Service tickets can provide material for offline password guessing. A request alone does
not prove recovery.

Sources: [A, K1, K2]  •  Source notes included with the set.

OBSERVE THE REQUEST. INVESTIGATE THE CONTEXT.
4769 ON THE DC
Requester • target service
Result • encryption type
COMPARE REQUESTS
Breadth • novelty

CORROBORATE
Source-process activity

The request event does not show offline password recovery.
TICKET ENCRYPTION TYPES • KEEP THE SCOPE EXPLICIT
0x17
RC4-HMAC
0x11
AES128
0x12
AES256
An RC4-only filter cannot claim AES coverage.
COLLECTION CHECK
Enable service-ticket auditing on domain
controllers. Preserve event version, source
address and encryption type. Validate what
the logged service identifier actually
represents.
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
Routine service requests are legitimate.
Low-volume targeting can evade breadth
rules. Do not exclude every principal or
service ending in $. No universal count
threshold is implied.
A ticket request is not proof of a cracked credential.

AUDITING PREREQUISITE
Configure Directory Service Access auditing
and a matching SACL on the domain object.
A SACL selects auditing; effective
permissions govern access. Relevant rights
may appear in separate events.
VALIDATE THE EXCEPTIONS
Verify approved principal–source relationships
with current inventory. Avoid blanket
account-name exclusions. An approved
source can be compromised. One matching
right does not prove credential extraction.
Preserve uncertain source attribution. Do not invent an IP
address.

TWO HUNTING VIEWS
Captured password-hash material can support authentication without the cleartext
password.

TWO EVIDENCE CLASSES • NOT A BINARY PtH CLASSIFIER
SOURCE-SIDE VIEW
4624
Type 9 • NewCredentials
LogonProcess: seclogo
Some implementations; also legitimate
alternate-credential workflows.
TARGET-SIDE VIEW
4624
Type 3 • Network
AuthenticationPackage: NTLM
Also appears during ordinary network
authentication.
Neither view proves PtH. Not every implementation produces both.
CORRELATE THE BEHAVIOR AND ITS AUTHORIZATION
Identity
Source process
Destination
Admin context
CORRELATION CHECK
Match the outbound identity, source process,
target and event time. Type 9
outbound-account fields may differ from the
local identity. Logon IDs are host-local, not
cross-host join keys.
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
Null Subject SID, zero key length or a missing
earlier logon does not establish hash reuse.
Check collection, retention and clock
alignment before interpreting absence.
Validate authorized administration.
NTLM uses challenge–response. The hash is not sent as a
password.

COLLECT PROCESS CONTEXT
Preserve source/target process GUIDs,
access rights and call trace. Correlate
process creation, signer/hash, ancestry and
available memory evidence. Validate
Sysmon filtering and sensor health.
INTERPRETATION LIMIT
Security and diagnostic tools may access
LSASS legitimately. An unresolved call trace
does not prove injection. Scope and review
exceptions; a familiar name, signer or
directory is not a universal safe exclusion.
Decode the access rights. Then establish provenance.
